originality.rationale: Seo and Slater (2017) give a general girth-at-least-five neighborhood-condition characterization. Cappelle et al. (2021/2022) give NP-completeness in separately planar-bipartite degree-five and planar-subcubic girth-nine classes; no full-one-subdivision-of-planar-cubic intersection case. The 1988 planar-cubic perfect-code hardness is expressly a prior premise, not claimed as new. Algebraic signature comparison derives a one-to-one code transfer and a new NP-completeness restriction. Relevant mathematical-literature searches returned no statement covering the combined assertion; absence from search is not proof of priority.
residual_risks: The earlier 1988 hardness theorem was invoked from explicit publisher abstract, without a full-text verification of its proof.

A paper under alternate descriptions (perfect codes in subdivisions, identifying sensors, efficient domination) may have anticipated the bridge; mathematical database searches do not prove uniqueness.
The 2017 high-girth characterization is a strong umbrella theorem; an unpublished or unindexed explicit reduction from planar cubic perfect codes may already exist.

value.rationale: The transfer is bijective and parsimonious, with an explicit inverse. It yields NP-completeness simultaneously on planar, bipartite, max-degree-three, girth-at-least-six graphs, strengthening previously separated restrictions, plus rigid code cardinality and an exact counting identity. These naturally motivated algorithmic and detection questions are not arbitrary small invariants.
